## [§1.1.c] Gym origin story — Facebook lead costs, supplements insight

So here's a quick story for you. So let me tell you how this all started. So this is me when I signed my first lease at $5,000 a month. That's me not knowing what I was doing. And this is where I slept, and that's my really fancy equipment that I was able to afford. Um, and so I heard about this thing called Facebook marketing, and things started going well. This is actually a picture that I sent to my dad after the first week of, uh, having my gym to show how many memberships. I actually was very proud of this, uh, which is kind of silly now that I look at it. It's like, I had like, whatever, 18 memberships. But I was super proud of this. I was, I had hustled all day to get that. And so the thing is, is that things started to grow. And so that was good. This was our, my one year. There's my little, my little dinky streamers 'cause that's what I could afford at the time. Um, but things were going well. Like, all my clients showed up, which was kind of sweet. Um, and we grew over to nine plus employees, so that was cool. Um, and I started to feel like I had it figured out. I was like, "I'm a businessman." And then, of course, Facebook slaps me, and they five X my cost per lead. And so what was once a money, you know, torrential hurricane or downpour turned into the Sahara Desert or whatever desert this is. Uh, and all I could think about was, you know, having to call my dad saying, "I'm gonna be... I'm a failure. This is actually didn't work. I didn't really know what I was doing." And that would've sucked, right? And so all I could think about was, "How can I afford to pay for more leads," right? Like, the business worked, everything was fine, it's just my cost per lead went up. And so I needed something that was immediate cash upfront, so I could pay off my credit card bill for the ad spend without going into debt. And so I want to highlight one key point right now is that two types of business owners. One type of business owner tries to keep figuring out and being upset about the things that are out of their control. If your, if CPMs, the cost per impression goes up on a platform, you can either afford the impressions or you can't. And you can beg, borrow, and steal and wish that the impression cost goes down, but it's not gonna change anything, right? Of course, you can make better ads, you can make better hooks, things like that. But fundamentally, my lead cost went up. So, you can either go out of business, or you can try and figure out a way to make more money per customer. And so that's what we did. All right. And so this is what happened. So I'm traveling home for the holidays. And I've got this layover somewhere, and I see a guy from college in the same waiting area. And I was like, "Oh, no shoot." I was like, "Hey, what's up, dude?" Uh, so we start chatting, and it turned out that he'd started a supplement business. And I was like, "Oh, okay. Kind of interesting." And so I was like, "Hey, so how do you make... how much do you make a month from your supplement company?" He's like, "Well, I got two locations. One does about 80,000 a month. The other's 130,000 a month." And I was like, "A month?" I was like, "Selling supplements?" And, uh, and I was like, "Hold on." I was like, "If this guy can make an extra 80,000 a month selling supplement without any members... I got a gym, he has no gym. I've got a gym with members, he doesn't have members." I was like, "I can definitely sell 20 grand a month with my members just to cover my costs." And so I put an order for supplements to resell at my gym. And at first, of course, no one bought, until one day I was able to make a sale. And then from that day and going forward, I began selling $200 per person in supplements, so about a hundred bucks in profit. And that $100 offset my cost of getting a new member in the door. And so I used to have to spend money to get the person in the door, and then sell them stuff and then wait to get, you know, recruit membership cost, et cetera. But here with the supplements, I could sell them supplements up front, and I made my cost to get the customer back. All right. So I was able to start spending way more money on ads again, because it paid for my advertising. And so it made all the new members and the cash they paid free, which was sweet. And so the moral is that I made another offer. And when I made another offer, I made more money. And so the outcome was I was able to get paid to get new customers. And I'll say that again. I was able to get paid to get new customers. So most people pay to get customers. I was getting paid to grow. And so my gyms grew. And so over time, I continued to get better and better at, at recombining the way I charged and structured my client journey to make more money than my competitors. And so I went from making like four to five to one, to making 30 to one and up. So like, every dollar I put in, I would get $30, $40 back on my marketing. And I'll show you how I did it. All right.
